utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-04-84-I, the Prosecutor against Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Good morning to you. Mr. Haradinaj, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure before I proceed any further that you can follow the proceedings in your own language or in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. [Previous translation continues] ... [In English] hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not receiving interpretation myself, and could you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Everything is okay. Translation is okay, and I'm hearing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If at any moment in the course -- during the proceedings you're not receiving interpretation, please draw my attention immediately. And the same applies to the other two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, good morning to you too. The same question: Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Brahimaj, good morning to you, and it's the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you receiving interpretation in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, you may sit down. Let's have appearances. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff. I represent the Prosecution today and I am accompanied by case manager, Hasan Younis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you and your team. Now, appearances for Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Rodney Dixon. I appear to represent Mr. Haradinaj. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And have you been appointed to represent him throughout all the proceedings or are you just a duty counsel for today, or the initial appearance, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm one of the lawyers who has been appointed to represent him in the proceedings from today and onwards. I'm not duty counsel, I'm appointed by the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Dixon. Good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Gregor Guy-Smith. I have been appointed as duty counsel at this time to represent Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir, and good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I am Richard Harvey and I have been appointed as duty counsel for this morning to represent Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you. Before I proceed any further, I wish to make one point very clear, and this is particularly addressed to the three accused, and that is that you, throughout the entire proceedings, you enjoy right to remain silent. Let me first give some details on the indictment. The three accused, that is, Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj, are included in the indictment with case number IT-04-84, which was signed on the 25th of February of this year. This indictment was confirmed by my colleague Judge Lord Iain Bonomy on the 4th of March, 2005. The indictment was made public by a decision of the same Judge, Lord Bonomy, of the 10th of March, 2005. Previous to that, the indictment and everything that accompanied it, particularly the warrant of arrest, was under seal. Accused Ramush Haradinaj and Lahi Brahimaj turned themselves in to the custody of this Tribunal and arrived at the seat of this Tribunal, as most of you know, last week, at precisely on the 9th of March of 2005. The third accused, Idriz Balaj, was transferred to The Hague later on the same day. There are the factual allegations which form the basis this indictment, which I will go through very briefly, and then I will explain what the three accused are accused -- are charged with. The indictment alleges that after the 24th of March of 1998, KLA forces under the command and control of accused Ramush Haradinaj, mounted a systematic campaign to seize control of the area between villages of Gllogjan and Decani and particularly the villages of Dubrave, Rznic, Ratis, and Dasinovac in order to drive ethnic Serbs out of the villages where they were living and that they also continued to launch attacks against the camp of refugees of Jablanica near Decani. This camp, according to the Prosecution, had been the target of similar KLA attacks as -- as since 1997. The indictment states that the KLA forces under the command and control of Ramush Haradinaj, including the Black Eagles under the direct control of Idriz Balaj, harassed, beat, or otherwise drove Serbian civilians and Roma/Egyptian civilians out of these villages and killed those civilians that remained behind or had refused to abandon their homes, and that they continued to mount similar attacks against the Serb and Roma civilians as well as Albanian civilians perceived as collaborators. The indictment further states that many abductions by KLA forces took place in the Dukagjin zone and that tens of civilians went missing. The indictment also alleges that the KLA forces, acting under the command and control of Ramush Haradinaj, had full control of the Operational Zone and did not tolerate the presence of any other Albanian factions fighting against the Serbs, such as the armed forces of the Republic of Kosovo. The indictment alleges also that in the second half of May, 1998, a makeshift detention centre was established at the KLA headquarters in Jablanica and that between then and August 1998, at least 16 non-combatants were detained, beaten, and tortured. One is known to have died while the others are still missing. The indictment also states that during the end or about -- round about the end of August and the beginning of September, 1998, Serb forces temporarily retook the area surrounding Gllogjan and that a Serbian forensic crime scene team conducted an investigation in the vicinity of the canal leading to the lake Radonjic, the Ekonomija farm in Rznic, and a road leading to Dasinovac where they identified at least 39 bodies and partial remains, human remains. Several of these remains have been identified as belonging to Serb, Roma, and civilian -- Albanian civilians who disappeared between April and September 1998 in the Dukadjin area. The indictment alleges also that as commander of the Dukadjin Operational Zone, Ramush Haradinaj ensured that the KLA forces under his control operated in a structured and disciplined manner, provided overall control of planning and organisation of operations and established a system whereby individuals were targeted for abduction, mistreatment, and murder, and whereby a systematic attack on vulnerable sections of the civilian population was carried out. The Prosecution alleges also that by excluding all rival KLA forces, Haradinaj secured power for his own troops within this -- his zone, and by attacking Serb forces in rural areas gave his own troops freedom to dominate and persecute vulnerable sections of the civilian population. Prosecution alleges that he used his own house as a centre of operations and used his other Haradinaj family member resources and the support of his family members to further the consolidation of his power and his persecution of civilians. The indictment alleges that Haradinaj appointed and maintained his co-accused in positions of responsibility and condoned and encouraged their criminal conduct and behaviour in such position. It further states that on some occasions, Haradinaj personally ordered, controlled, and participated in the beatings of persons detained by his forces and taking no active part in hostilities, and on other occasions by his presence and tacit or overt approval of such criminal conduct he, in his position of commander, encouraged and instigated criminal behaviour by members of his own forces. The indictment also alleges that Haradinaj controlled the continued detention or release or medical treatment of persons held by the KLA in his Operational Zone, that he participated in the abduction of persons who were later found murdered, and that on at least one occasion he gave his tacit approval as commander for detained persons to be executed. The indictment alleges that as commander of the Black Eagles special unit, Idriz Balaj worked closely with Haradinaj and provided direct operational support for his activities and that he personally and using soldiers under his command repeatedly abducted, beat, mutilated, tortured, and murdered civilians and detained persons taking no active part in the hostilities. In addition, the Prosecution alleges that he raped a Roma/ Egyptian woman, that he personally visited the Jablanica detention centre, mutilated and tortured a prisoner there, and by his presence as a KLA commander provided his tacit or overt approval for persecution and criminal conduct by other KLA soldiers. The Prosecution alleges also that he knew that the facility was operating in a persecutory and criminal fashion. The indictment also states that the accused Balaj attempted to prevent inquiry into and to conceal the abduction and murder of civilians and disposal of bodies at Radonjic lake. The indictment finally alleges also that as deputy command of the Dukadjin operative staff and the responsible local KLA commander, accused Lahi Brahimaj ran the KLA detention facility at Jablanica, ordered, supervised and participated in the beating, torture and murder of persons who were detained there, and that he personally abducted one civilian and took him to the Jablanica detention facility where he was repeatedly beaten, and then personally took him from the detention facility to a potential place of execution. Those are the factual -- that is the factual background of the indictment. The Prosecution alleges that you, Ramush Haradinaj, are also known as Smajl, and that you were born on the 3rd of July, 1968 in Gllogjan in the municipality of Decani and that at all times relevant to the indictment you were a commander of the Kosovo Liberation Army, which I will refer to as the KLA and which I have been referring to as the KLA, and that in addition you had overall command of the KLA forces in one of the KLA operational zones called Dukadjin. Prosecution alleges that you were one of the most senior KLA leaders in Kosovo. This Operational Zone, according to the Prosecutor, encompassed the municipalities of Pec, Decani, Djakovica, and part of the municipalities of Istok and Kline. As regards you, Mr. Balaj, according to the indictment you are also known as Troger or Trogeri in your language, or Lieutenant, and that you were born on the 23rd of August, 1971 in Iglarevo in the municipality of Klina in Kosovo. The Prosecution alleges that at all times relevant to the indictment you were a member of the KLA and acted as the commander of the special unit known as the Black Eagles. The Prosecution alleges that you were subordinate to co-accused Ramush Haradinaj, reported directly to him, and worked closely with him. As regards you, Mr. Brahimaj, according to the indictment you are also known as Maxhup, or Gipsy, and that you were born on the 26th of January, 1970 in Jablanica in the municipality of Djakovica in Jablanica. The Prosecution alleges that you are a close relative of co-accused Ramush Haradinaj and that at all times relevant to the indictment you were a member of the KLA and acted as the deputy commander of the Dukagjin Operative Staff or as the Dukadjin zone contact person to the KLA General Staff. The Prosecution alleges also that you were stationed in Jablanica and you were subordinate to co-accused Ramush Haradinaj, reported directly to him, and worked closely with him. Basically, when we come to the charges that are being brought against you in the indictment, the Prosecution alleges as a mode of criminal responsibility that of a joint criminal enterprise, a mode of committing of which the three accused, according to Madam Prosecutor, were members. This joint criminal enterprise, according to the indictment, came into existence on or before April 1998, and its raison d'etre was the consolidation of total control of the KLA over the KLA Operational Zone of Dukadjin by attacking and persecuting certain sections of the civilian population there, namely the unlawful removal of Serb civilians from that area, and the forcible, violent suppression of any real or perceived form of collaboration with the Serbs by Albanian or Roma civilians there. The criminal purpose included the intimidation, abduction, imprisonment, beating, torture, and murder of targeted civilians. In sum, accused Ramush Haradinaj is charged with 17 counts of crimes against humanity grounded on Article 5 of this Tribunal's Statute, and with an additional 20 counts of violations of the laws or customs of war grounded on Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. The other two accused, Idriz Balaj and Lahi Brahimaj, are both charged with 16 counts of crimes against humanity based under or on Article 5 of the Statute, and with 19 counts of violations of the laws or customs of war under Article 3 of the Statute. According to the Prosecutor, all crimes alleged in the indictment occurred between the 1st of March of 1998 and the 30th of September of 1998 in the territory of Kosovo in the former Yugoslavia and were directed against the Serb civilian population and those members of the Albanian and Roma/Egyptian civilian population in Decani, Pec, Djakovica, Istok, and Kline municipalities perceived to be collaborators and not supporting the KLA. By an order dated the 9th of March of this year, the Vice-President of this Tribunal, Judge Fausto Pocar, assigned this case to Trial Chamber II, of which I am the Presiding Judge. Two days later, on the 11th March 2005, I designated myself as the Pre-Trial Judge for the purposes of this, today's initial appearance of the three accused. I will now pass on to the procedural proper part of the initial appearance of the three accused pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal, and then having done that, I will move to perhaps what is the most important formality of this appearance, and I will formally charge the three accused and ask them to enter a plea. Mr. Haradinaj, would you please stand up. It is my duty as Pre-Trial Judge to make sure that you are represented legally here, and that's unless, of course, you want to conduct your own defence. I take it from what I heard Mr. Dixon state earlier on that you are represented not only for the purposes of this initial appearance but that proceedings are in place for the assigning of counsel for the purpose of the rest of the proceedings. Are you happy with the situation as it obtains now? In other words, are you happy with the representation that you have at your disposal at the moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. You may sit down. Mr. Balaj. The same question to you. I heard earlier on Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith state that he's been appointed as duty counsel, that is, in another words, he's been assigned to represent you for the purpose of this initial appearance only. I would like a feedback from you on this. I want to know if you are happy with the situation or whether you would like to make any representations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the time Mr. Guy-Smith is the one. We'll see how it develops in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down. Mr. Brahimaj. Same question to you. I heard earlier on Mr. Harvey state that he's been appointed as duty counsel. That's for the purpose of today's initial appearance only. Do you have anything to say, state about that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with the appointment of Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Now, the next thing that I have to do is to go through again procedural routine by confirming your identity basically. Mr. Haradinaj, could you please stand up. Could you give me, please, your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next question I'm going to ask you, you're free not to answer if you like because it may be an element of proof later on: Do you have any nicknames or are you known by any nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only my name Ramush Haradinaj. That's how I'm known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you give me your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Gllogjan in the Decan municipality in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I am going to ask you for your address, your last address before you came over here. If you prefer to give it in private session, we will go in private session for a while and you can give me your address. I don't think this is something that the public ought to be familiar with. It's your preference. I mean, you tell me what your preference is. Or your counsel. Mr. Dixon, if you want to consult.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could I have one moment to speak to Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for the explanation. I prefer to do it in a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are in open session. What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is your family informed about your transfer and detention here in The Hague, your transfer to and detention in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you like me as an officer of this Tribunal to inform anyone of your transfer and detention here in this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no need for that. Everybody has been informed because everything is possible to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Haradinaj. You may sit down. Mr. Balaj. Same routine with you. Could I have your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Idriz Balaj, born on the 23rd of August, 1971.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a while, and Mr. Balaj will give us his last address before he came over here to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And your nationality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are the members of your family aware that you've been transferred here to The Hague and that you are being kept in a state of detention in the United Nations Detention Unit in Scheveningen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you like me as an officer of this Tribunal to inform anyone of your presence here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to raise your voice a little bit. Is his microphone switched on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you what? Do you require me to inform anyone of your presence here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Brahimaj, same procedure. Could you please give me your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before you proceed further, may I just have one word with my client on that point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to advise him on that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you whether you have any nickname. You're free to -- not to answer that question, like every other question, for that matter. Would you like to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. My name is Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But do you have any nicknames? Are you known by any nicknames? I didn't receive any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. When were you born? Your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born in the village of Jablanica, Gjakove municipality, Kosovo, on the 26th of January, 1970.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And are the members of your family informed about your transfer to and your detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you like me as an officer of this Tribunal to inform any person of your presence and state of detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] no thank you. Everybody knows about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please sit down. Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj and Mr. Brahimaj, your arraignment and initial appearance here today before me entails a number of rights. These rights are enshrined in our Statute and to an extent also repeated in our Rules. I want you to be fully aware of these rights, and for that reason I'm going to ask Mr. Registrar to stand up and read out to you Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute of this Tribunal, which spell out one by one all these rights. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 20 commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. "1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker slow down, please, the interpreters are asking.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: "-- rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Registrar, the interpreters would like you to slow down, so I would suggest that you start again because they have lost track completely. This is a Statute. I suppose you should have a copy of it available. We are reading from Rule 20 and Rule 21. But please do slow down. Also, I take it there was a problem or were you just referring to what the interpreters --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was referring to what the interpreters raised Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Commencing again, Article 20 commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. "1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. 2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him and transferred to the International Tribunal. 3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. 4. The hearings shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with its Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Article 21, rights of the accused: 1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. 2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the Statute. 3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present Statute. 4. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality: (a) To be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; (b) To have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; (c) To be tried without undue delay; (d) To be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing; to be informed, if he does not have legal assistance, of this right; and to have legal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. assistance assigned to him, in any case where the interests of justice so require, and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; (e) To examine, or have examined, the witnesses against him and to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; (f) To have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal; (g) Not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Brahimaj, could you stand up again, please. You did not give us your last address before you arrived here in The Hague, so let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Mr. Haradinaj, could you stand up, please. You heard -- you heard the Registrar read out in full Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute of this Tribunal which lay down these rights that you enjoy. They are procedural and substantive rights as an accused before this Tribunal. Do you understand the importance of these rights?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you received the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of its contents and do you understand the import of the charges -- charges that are brought against you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You may sit down for the time being. Mr. Balaj, could you stand up, please. I have the same questions for you. First, you heard the Registrar read out Articles 20 and 21 as regards the rights that you enjoy as an accused before this Tribunal. Do you understand the importance of these rights?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you received the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you understand the -- its contents? Are you aware of what you're being charged with and the facts that are alleged against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have read it, and I have everything -- I am aware of everything in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Balaj. You may sit down. Mr. Brahimaj, the same questions to you. You heard the Registrar read out Articles 20 and 21 from the Statute of this Tribunal spelling out your procedure and substantive rights as an accused before this Tribunal. Do you understand the importance of these rights?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you been served with the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of the charges, the nature of the charges, and the underlying factual allegations contained in this indictment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you understand completely what you're being charged with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Now, according to the Rules I should proceed with the reading out of the indictment in full unless, of course, there is a waiver forthcoming from the accused. There are three accused here, and I need to know where we stand on this. I will start with you, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On behalf of Mr. Haradinaj, there's no need to read the indictment out in full. It's only necessary to read out the charges so he can enter his pleas of not guilty. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Dixon. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, there is no need to read out the indictment out in full, only the charges so Mr. Balaj is in a position to enter his pleas of not guilty at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The same goes for Mr. Brahimaj. He fully understands the nature and content of the indictment and is ready to enter his pleas of not guilty [Realtime transcript read in error "guilty"] forthwith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Now, the procedure will be as follows: I will --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise I do see that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The transcript actually says "his pleas of guilty forthwith" and I would like that to be changed forthwith to "not guilty."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Harvey. That goes, for the record, there is exactly the opposite of what there should be in the transcript. Mr. Harvey said that his client will be pleading not guilty. So I will not be reading out the indictment in full although I will be going through all the charges or the counts one by one, but very briefly. I wish to makes it very clear to the three accused that pursuant to Rule 62(A)(iii) of our Rules you have a right to enter a plea of guilty or a plea of not guilty or even to remain silent on each count today. If you do not enter a plea, in other words, if you remain silent or if you prefer not to enter a plea today, our Rules allow for an interval of time of 30 days within which you can then enter a plea. 30 days from today. If you don't enter a plea by the end of those 30 days, I will then enter a plea myself on your behalf, a plea of not guilty. I take it that you have all had an opportunity to discuss with your counsel whether you will be entering a plea today and what kind of a plea you will be entering. If it's -- if that's not the case, please let me know now. I don't see a reaction, which means that I take it you have discussed this with your counsel. Mr. Haradinaj, as I explained earlier on, you have more charges than the other co-accused. Basically, the first count and the second count relate to you only. So I will be starting with you and limitedly, for the time being, to counts 1 and 2. I will tell you the nature of these counts, the charge that is brought against you under each of these two counts, and then I will ask you how you would like to plead to these charges, and please tell me plead not guilty or guilty or I prefer not to plead, as the case may be. Mr. Haradinaj, the first count that is brought against you under this indictment is one of persecution, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is charging you with other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute of this Tribunal, which is also a crime against humanity. How would you like to plead to this first count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Registrar, at the end of this exercise I will tell you exactly what to put on record. Thank you. The second count which is levelled, brought against you, Mr. Haradinaj, in the indictment is one of cruel treatment, being a violation of the laws or customs of war, and this is punishable under Article 3 of this Statute of the Tribunal. How do you wish to plead to this second count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now I would ask Mr. Balaj and Mr. Brahimaj to stand up as well. Now we go -- we start from count 3 and go straight to the end. The charges from count 3 to the last count are common to the three of you, so the way I am going to do it is that I will state what the charge is, and then I will ask you one after the other how you would like to plead to each of these counts. In the third count of the indictment, with which you are all charged, the Prosecution is alleging that you are criminally responsible of having committed the crime of persecution, which is a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal, and alternatively, it's being alleged that you are criminally responsible for the crime of deportation pursuant to Article 5(d) and also a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to 5 -- Article 5(i) of the Statute, both crimes being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, with regard to this third count, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this fourth count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead to this fourth count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We go to the fifth count, and the fifth count is -- contains a charge of persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, Prosecution is bringing against you a charge of imprisonment pursuant to Article 5(e), and a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, all being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this fifth count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead to this fifth count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Brahimaj, how do you wish to plead to this fifth count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. We come to the sixth count and the sixth count contains a charge of cruel treatment, that is being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Brahimaj, how would you like to plead to this sixth count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Count 7. Count 7 is a charge of persecution. Again it might all seem to be a repetition here but the facts alleged in this count amounting to persecution are different in each case. Count 7 contains a charge of persecution being a crime against humanity which is punishable, as I said earlier on, under Articles 5 (h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is alleging that you committed murder pursuant to Article 5(a) of the Statute, this being a crime against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this seventh count; guilty or not guilty?

Then we come to the eighth count, and the eighth count contains a charge of murder as being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this eighth count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead to this eighth count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Brahimaj, how do you wish to plead to this eighth count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ninth count, which is one of persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Entirely not [Realtime transcript read in error "guilty"] guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 11th count again contains a charge of persecution against the three of you. utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Your Honour. With regard to the last plea that my client entered, I believe that we have a bit of a problem. That is on line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "Entirely guilty" it says. It should be "entirely not guilty." Please, I ask you to be kind enough to follow the transcript because I can't do this exercise and follow the transcript at the same time. I do thank you. I'm very grateful for your remark, Mr. Guy-Smith, and I'm sure that the record at the end will reflect that the accused entered a plea of not guilty and not one of guilty. When I say "the accused," I'm referring to Mr. Balaj. We come to the 12th count, which is one of murder, being a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 12th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

Alternatively, the Prosecution is charging you with murder and other inhumane acts, being crimes against humanity and pursuant to Article 5(a) and 5(i) respectively of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 15th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the 17th count is one persecution, being a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. Or alternatively, the Prosecutor is bringing against you a charge of murder pursuant to Article 5(a) and a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, all these being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 18th count is a charge of murder, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how would you like to plead to this 18th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. We come to the 19th count, which is one of persecution punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is bringing against you a charge of murder pursuant to Article 5(a) and a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, all these being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how would you like to plead to this 19th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 20th count is one of murder being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, what's your plea to this 20th charge; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the 21st count is one of persecution, being a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is alleging murder against you pursuant to article 5(a) of the Statute of this Tribunal, all these being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 21st count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we come to the 22nd count, which is one of murder being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how would you like to plead to this 22nd count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the 23rd count is one of persecution, which is a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. Alternatively, the Prosecution is alleging or charging you with murder pursuant to Article 5(a), and the charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, which are also crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 23rd count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We come to the 24th count, which is one of murder as being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 24th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Come to the 25th count, which is one of persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. Alternatively, the Prosecution is alleging murder, which is charged against you pursuant to Article 5(a) of the Statute, these being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how would you like to plead to this 25th count of persecution; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the 26th count is one of murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. 27th count is one of persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. Alternatively, the Prosecution is charging you with other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute. All these are crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Entirely not guilty. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. 28th count is of one is cruel treatment, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 28th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. 29th count, which is also one of cruel treatment and also being a violation of the laws or customs of war, of course based on different facts. This is punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 29th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead to this 29th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Brahimaj, the same question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we come to count 30 which contains a charge of murder, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, what is your plea?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 31st count is one of persecution, this being a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is alleging that you committed murder pursuant to Article 5(a) of the Statute and the charge is bringing also against you a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, all these being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. 32nd count is one of murder, this being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Balaj, how do you wish to plead to this 32nd count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we come to 33rd count, which is one of cruel treatment as being a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 33rd count?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 34th count is one of persecution, a crime against humanity punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. Alternatively, the Prosecution is charging you with other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, which is also a crime against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 34th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And the 35th count against you is a charge of persecution, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of this Tribunal. Alternatively, the Prosecution is charging you with rape pursuant to Article 5(g) and a charge of other inhumane acts pursuant to Article 5(i) of the Statute, both being crimes against humanity. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 35th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Count 36. This is a charge of rape, being a violation of the laws or customs of war, which is punishable under Article 2 and Article 3 of the Statute of this Tribunal according to the indictment. I'm not going into whether Article 2 is pleaded against you in this case or not. Mr. Haradinaj, I'm sure your lawyers will take this up later on. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 36th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We come to the last count which is the 37th count, which is one of cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Mr. Haradinaj, how do you wish to plead to this 37th count; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Registrar, I should like to ask you to enter for the record that the three accused pleaded not guilty to each and every one of the counts brought against them in the indictment. I thank you. Having said so, I wish to inform you, Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj, that at any time from now onwards you are entitled to change your plea. You can change your plea to one of guilty to all the charges or you can change your plea to one of guilty to some of the charges. That's up to you. Before I proceed, I also wish to draw your attention to one of the Rules that we have, and that is Rule 63, and I'm going to read it out to you so that you will be fully aware of it, particularly since some of you do not yet have counsel assigned to them. Rule 63, first paragraph, states: "Questioning by the Prosecutor of an accused, including after the initial appearance, shall not proceed without the presence of counsel unless the accused has voluntarily and expressly agreed to proceed without counsel being present. If the accused subsequently expresses a desire to have counsel, questioning shall thereupon cease and shall only resume when the accused's counsel is present." The second paragraph of Rule 63 states that "The questioning, including any waiver of the right to counsel, shall be audio-recorded or video-recorded in accordance with the procedure provided for in Rule 43. The Prosecutor shall at the beginning of the questioning caution the accused in accordance with Rule 42(A)(iii)," which basically the Prosecution needs to caution you that you have the right to remain silent, no one can force you to incriminate yourselves, and that anything you may say may be used in evidence. Mr. Haradinaj, Mr. Balaj, and Mr. Brahimaj, I will very soon after this sitting appoint a pre-trial Judge who will schedule a Status Conference to be held within 120 days from today pursuant to Rule 65 bis (A) of the Rules of Procedure of this Tribunal. The purpose of the Status Conference is twofold. First, it is to organise exchanges between the parties and facilitate expeditious preparation for trial. Secondly, the Pre-Trial Judge will have an opportunity to see you in person and to ensure that you are being treated well and to be made aware of any complaints or requests that you may have. You will later on be informed of the exact date of this Status Conference which will be fixed by the Pre-Trial Judge that I will appoint. In addition, I will be giving instructions to the Registrar to start preparing a date for the trial when appropriate. Of course, please do not interpret what I have just said that the trial will start in a very short time. There will be all the time needed required to be taken first before a trial date can be fixed. But it will be fixed at the earliest opportunity. In the meantime, I have signed an order to the effect that you will remain in custody for the time being. I wish to advise you that in terms of Rule 65 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you may at any time file an application for provisional release which will of course be dealt with after hearing what the Prosecution has to say. I'm sure that now and later your respective Defence counsel will be able to assist you on this. I turn to my left, and madam, I wish to remind you that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure you have 30 days from today to make available to the respective Defence counsel in a language which the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought by your office. If there are any problems or that if you anticipate any problems in regard, please speak now.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution is aware of its obligation and will act accordingly. However, I have, of course, inquired with the translation section. It will be difficult for them, given their limited resources, but I'm quite confident that we still have everything in the language that the accused understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Then there is obviously the question of Defence counsel, because I cannot anticipate how long it's going to take the Registrar to assign counsel to each and every one of the accused. I mean, from the looks of it, it's only Mr. Dixon that is -- appears on the horizon for the time being. So that may occasion the need for an extension of the -- of the time if there is no counsel unless the parties -- the accused themselves wish to have these documents delivered to them personally, but we'll come to that or the Pre-Trial Judge that I will appoint will -- will deal with that in due course. I thank you, madam. I wish to remind also the three accused and respective duty counsel present here that pursuant to Rule 72(A) of our Rules, the Defence has a period of 30 days for the filing of any preliminary pleas, preliminary motions. Once, however, you ever been served with all the supporting material and the basis of the indictment in accordance with Rule 66 mentioned earlier. So I don't need to expand or explain this. I'm pretty much sure that you are fully aware of this. We come to the close. Madam Prosecutor, is there any matter that you would like to raise at the moment, at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Is there any matter that the Defence for Mr. Haradinaj or the accused himself, for that matter, wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour did mention Rule 65 and provisional release. There will be no application made at this hearing today, but I did wish to inform the Court that such an application will be made for Mr. Haradinaj's provisional release in the future. I will also speak to my learned colleagues from the Prosecution about this to move the matter forward as quickly as possible. The basis for the application will be that his case is entirely unprecedented for a serving Prime Minister to immediately, once he heard about the indictment, resign from his position on the same day and to voluntarily hand himself over to the United Nations and the ICTY. He has cooperated fully and within the space of a few days has arrived here in The Hague. Your Honour, there will be a formal motion submitted setting out these grounds, together with the necessary guarantees, in the near future. I just wish to bring it to the Court's attention that that is the first application that will be made on his behalf as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Dixon. I will wait for that motion. That, of course, is something which will be dealt with by the full Trial Chamber. Is there any matter that Defence counsel for Mr. Balaj or the accused himself wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, there is. There are two things I wish to inform the Court as well the Prosecutor of. In my conversations was Mr. Balaj I have informed him of his right to have counsel present at all proceedings, and it is my understanding and my interpretation of the rule with regard to any questioning that might occur that during my tenure as duty counsel, I am that counsel and would inform any individuals who may seek to have any kind of interview with my client that they may not do so unless I am first informed of such a thing and then we'll make a determination whether or not it's appropriate. With regard to the issues concerning Rule 72, I do appreciate precisely what Your Honour has said. There are some concerns, however, that do exist, and they have arisen before and I just wish to alert you to those potential difficulties. If I remain in the position that I am now and my status changes, then I am more than happy to undertake any motions that need to be filed in the initial phases after obtaining complete disclosure of those supporting documents. However, I think it imprudent and would be filing a motion evidencing such concern if by that time permanent counsel does not exist for Mr. Balaj because I believe that permanent counsel is in a better position, looking at the entirety of the case, to make a determination what appropriate motions should be filed. It's not only a legal matter but also a matter of strategy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Guy-Smith, I wouldn't preempt any issues for the time being. I am not in a position to -- to know when counsel will be assigned to your client and who will be assigned to your client. Obviously everything will rotate on that as a factor plus the date or the time when the Prosecution would fulfil its obligations under Rule 66.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if there is need for extensions, obviously the last thing that you should think of is that the Trial Chamber would be unreasonable in -- in considering your motions or those of your successor if there will be a successor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And I turn to you, Mr. Harvey. Is there any matter that you or, for that matter, your client would like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I would say at this stage is that with reference to the possibility of an application for pre-trial release, Your Honour has already said clearly on the record that my client voluntarily surrendered himself the moment the indictment was made public and I do anticipate that at some stage application will be made in that respect. In addition, I would echo exactly what Mr. Guy-Smith has just said. I am currently duty counsel and until any other counsel is appointed by my client or on his behalf, I have advised him of his right not to be questioned by anybody on behalf of the Prosecution and I would expect that the normal courtesies would be extended; in other words, that nobody would seek to interview my client without first approaching me and informing me of their intention to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Haradinaj, could you stand up, please. You've been here a few days. I would like to know or to make sure that you have been treated well during your stay here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything has been fine, and I've been treated with dignity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Is there any complaint -- is there any complaint that you would like to make or are there any concerns, could be also health concerns that you would like me to be aware of?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED HARADINAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The health service and everything has been of the highest service. There is nothing in particular I wish to point to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Balaj, again I want to make sure that since your arrival here in The Hague you have been treated well. That's my first question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there anything that you would like to tell me, any complaints, any requests, except to send you home?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Brahimaj, the same question to you: Have you been treated well since your arrival here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And do you have any complaints or any remarks or any special requests that you would like to address to me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. That brings today's initial appearance to an end. Next there will be, as I explained earlier, the appointment by myself of the Pre-Trial Judge and of course the first Status Conference which you expect to happen within 120 days starting from today. I thank you all. Good morning.
